caption: The drawing depicts a formal garden layout with a rectangular composition, divided into several distinct sections by paths. The central area is divided into four smaller squares, each containing symmetrical designs with green, pink, purple, and yellow colors representing different types of plants or flowers; two of these squares feature intricate geometric and circular patterns, while the other two are divided into four quadrants with corner plantings. To the bottom left is a rectangular plot with rows of alternating green and yellow colors, likely representing rows of crops or vegetables. Large green rectangular sections are positioned on the left, right, and lower right of the plan, depicting open grassy areas or lawns. The top border of the image has a band of pencil-like drawings of fruits, vegetables, and flowers. The perimeter is enclosed by a brown fence or wall, with white gate structures with peaked roofs at two points along the right side. There is a pink-colored path system that divides the sections and leads to the gates, and an orange-tan triangular shape occupies the top right corner, likely representing a building or roof. In the lower right corner, blue text reads, "The Stuyvesant Garden from the Castello Plan," with the number "1660" in blue next to it.
title: Peter Stuyvesant Garden
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
